subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Rammed Earth: Walls Pounded Into Place
description: A fast breakdown of Rammed Earth: Walls Pounded Into Place for builders.

hook.text: Parts of the Great Wall of China are not stone. They're compacted dirt — rammed earth.

buildup.text: Workers pour damp soil into forms and pound it with heavy tools until it's dense as soft rock.

discovery.text: Rammed earth walls regulate temperature naturally. They absorb heat during the day and release it at night.

twist.text: Modern rammed earth uses cement additives and reaches strengths comparable to low-grade concrete.

climax.text: Luxury homes in Australia and the US now use rammed earth for its beauty and thermal performance.

punchline.text: Pound dirt hard enough and it becomes a wall.

quiz.question: What thermal advantage does rammed earth provide?
options: It reflects sunlight to keep buildings cool all day
It absorbs heat during the day and releases it at night
It blocks all heat transfer like modern insulation foam
